successors.note: Formed 18 March 1948 from Alwar, Bharatpur, Dholpur and Karauli; merged into Greater Rajasthan on 15 May 1949 (Matsya Union page). Bharatpur acceded to India on 15 August 1947 (infobox). matsya-union needs a dossier.

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe. Suraj Mal's "Jat State embraced the districts of Agra, Dholpur, Mainpuri, Hathras, Aligarh, Etawa, Mirat, Rohtak..." with Mathura, Farrukhnagar, Mewat and Gurgaon; Agra was taken on 12 June 1761 and held "until 1774". The page gives no date for each district (all within 1755-1763) and no area; the circles about the district towns give about 49,000 km2 plus the core. The Jat state at its peak also covered "Delhi" in the Bharatpur State page's words, which is not drawn (the 1764 sack was a raid).

The core about Bharatpur and Deeg stands in for 1774-1948; the intermediate extent is a gap (the Matsya Union page gives no area).

ledger.note: 18 November 1722: Badan Singh founds the Bharatpur state. "The state was founded by Maharaja Badan Singh in 1722"; infobox "Established: 18 November 1722". The page names no region; Bharatpur and Deeg are my reading.

region.text: the districts of Agra, Dholpur, Mainpuri, Hathras, Aligarh, Etawah, Meerut, Rohtak, Mathura, Farrukhnagar, Mewat and Gurgaon

ledger.note: 1755-1763: bridging, page silent on dates. The Suraj Mal page lists the districts of the Jat state (Agra, Dholpur, Mainpuri, Hathras, Aligarh, Etawa, Mirat, Rohtak, Mathura, Farrukhnagar, Mewat, Gurgaon) and says the state "reached its highest extent" in his reign (1755-1763); the Bharatpur page puts the zenith in the 1760s. The lands were held before by the Mughals, Rohillas, Marathas and others; the counterpart is nominal. Dated 1761 with Agra.
12 June 1761: Suraj Mal takes Agra. "Thus after a siege of one month, Suraj Mal captured Agra Fort on 12 June 1761."

minus.text: the districts of Agra, Dholpur, Mainpuri, Hathras, Aligarh, Etawah, Meerut, Rohtak, Mathura, Farrukhnagar, Mewat and Gurgaon

region.text: the Jat districts other than the Bharatpur core

ledger.note: 1774: bridging, page silent. The pages say nothing about the loss of Mathura, Aligarh, Meerut and the other districts of the Jat zenith; by 1805 the Jat state held only "his possessions, including Deeg". Dated with the fall of Agra; the counterpart is nominal (Najaf Khan of Delhi and the Marathas took them at unknown dates).
18 February 1774: Mirza Najaf Khan retakes Agra. The Jats held Agra until 1774, "when Mirza Najaf Khan retook it on 18 February 1774".

region.text: Bharatpur and Deeg, the Jat country of the Sinsinwar clan

ledger.note: 2 January 1805: Lake begins the siege of Bharatpur. "The siege took place between 2 January and 22 February 1805"; Ranjit Singh had come "out openly on Holkar's side after the defeat of Monson".

region.text: Bharatpur and Deeg, the Jat country of the Sinsinwar clan

ledger.note: 22 February 1805: the Jats beat off the British. Lake's forces "were repulsed four times in their attempts to storm the fortress"; Ranjit Singh then accepted the British offer and paid an indemnity, which "allowed him to retain all his possessions, including Deeg".

region.text: Bharatpur and Deeg, the Jat country of the Sinsinwar clan

ledger.note: 9 December 1825: Combermere besieges Bharatpur on behalf of the boy Balwant Singh. The page gives the siege dates as 9 December 1825 to 18 January 1826; Combermere "reached Bharatpore on the 10th".

region.text: Bharatpur and Deeg, the Jat country of the Sinsinwar clan

ledger.note: 18 January 1826: the fortress is stormed. "until on 18 January 1826 its fortress was stormed and captured" (British victory); Balwant Singh, recognised by the Governor-General, is confirmed; the Bharatpur State page calls the state a British protectorate from then. The page mentions no territory ceded.

region.text: Bharatpur and Deeg, the Jat country of the Sinsinwar clan

ledger.note: 18 March 1948: Bharatpur joins the Matsya Union with Alwar, Dholpur and Karauli. "formed on 18 March 1948 by the merger of four erstwhile princely states"; merged into Greater Rajasthan on 15 May 1949.

wars.name: Jat conquests under Suraj Mal

zones.text: the districts of Agra, Dholpur, Mainpuri, Hathras, Aligarh, Etawah, Meerut, Rohtak, Mathura, Farrukhnagar, Mewat and Gurgaon

wars.outcome: Suraj Mal took Agra (12 June 1761) and the districts about it and Delhi; the Jat state reached its highest extent in his reign. Delhi was attacked in 1753 ("On 16 May Suraj Mal under Safdar Jang attacked Delhi") and sacked in 1764 under Jawahar Singh.
wars.note: The Suraj Mal page says "Maharaja Surajmal conquered Delhi on 10 May 1753" only in a note.

zones.text: Bharatpur and Deeg, the Jat country of the Sinsinwar clan

wars.outcome: Jat-Maratha defensive victory: four assaults failed; Ranjit Singh paid an indemnity and kept all his possessions including Deeg.

wars.name: Siege of Bharatpur (1825-1826)

wars.outcome: British victory: the fortress was stormed on 18 January 1826 and Balwant Singh confirmed; the page names no cession.

certainty.note: The pages give districts, forts and sieges but no boundary at any date; the extent after 1774 is not described. Circles around the district towns stand in.

notes: Six pages opened (Bharatpur State, Suraj Mal, Siege of Bharatpur and its 1805 and 1825-1826 articles, Matsya Union). The Bharatpur State page gives no infobox area, so the area check is not possible; the zenith shape measures about 49,000 km2 plus the core. The pages do not date the loss of the Jat districts after 1774 or say what the state held in 1805-1948 beyond Bharatpur and Deeg (core shape is a floor); nor the tribute to Scindia ("first a tributary of the House of Scindia"). Bharatpur and the British: "became a British protectorate" after 1826 on the page (citation needed) and a princely state after 1805; british-empire (sa-06) should record the vassal_start (1805 or 1826 per that dossier's reading) to 1947. Counterpart needing a dossier: matsya-union (1948-49, Rajasthan group). Contradictions on the page: Sujan Singh's succession 1750 or 1756; the 1805 treaty described as making Bharatpur a princely state. Gazetteer lacks Dholpur, Mainpuri, Hathras as places; coordinates used.
